security_audit.summary: Six shell-execution alerts, the dynamic-import alert, and the entropy heuristic are false positives caused by Markdown fences, Go syntax, and readable Chinese text. The curl instruction is genuine outbound network access, and the guide also relies on a moving dependency selector and mutable remote documentation. No credential access, obfuscation, destructive behavior, or direct prompt injection was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace @v1 with an exact reviewed release and instruct users to inspect go.mod and go.sum before accepting changes.
Pin documentation to a reviewed commit or release, remove automatic retrieval, and tell agents to treat fetched text as untrusted reference material.

static_findings.pattern: [HEURISTIC] High file entropy (6.09 bits) - possible binary/encrypted content

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 12-17 contain a static Go import block in a fenced example. There is no dynamic import expression or executable loader.
The backticks are Markdown delimiters around a documented go get command, not Ruby or shell command substitution. The Markdown file does not execute the command.
Line 11 is the opening fence for a Go code example. It does not invoke a shell or Ruby interpreter.
Line 18 closes a Markdown code fence. It is formatting syntax and cannot execute an external command.
Line 20 opens a fenced Go example containing library calls. The fence is not shell backtick execution.
Line 33 closes the Go example's Markdown fence. No command execution mechanism is present.
Line 38 is a Markdown fence labeling the following example as Bash. The fence itself does not execute a command.
The documented curl command makes an outbound request and follows redirects to retrieve mutable remote text. The destination appears to be the library's documentation domain, limiting the severity.
SKILL.md is fully readable UTF-8 Markdown containing Chinese prose and short Go examples. It contains no binary, encrypted, encoded, or intentionally obscured payload.

content.value_statement: Repetitive collection transformations and helper logic can obscure Go application code. This skill shows concise samber/lo patterns for collections, errors, concurrency, pointers, and related utilities.
actual_capabilities: Provides the Go command for adding samber/lo version 1.
Shows imports for the core, parallel, mutable, and iterator packages.
Demonstrates Filter, Map, Find, Uniq, GroupBy, and Must with short examples.
Explains when Must can panic and where initialization use is appropriate.
Points to the upstream function list and warns that it may differ from released versions.
limitations: Requires Go 1.18 or later because samber/lo uses generics.
Covers only a small selection of library functions.
Does not compare performance or allocations with native Go loops.
The remote function list may describe unreleased behavior and requires version verification.

use_cases.title: Refactor Collection Pipelines
use_cases.description: Replace repetitive slice filtering, mapping, deduplication, lookup, and grouping logic with focused generic helpers.

use_cases.title: Review Helper Usage
use_cases.description: Check whether samber/lo calls preserve behavior, expose missing cases, and use panic-based helpers only where intentional.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Patterns
use_cases.description: Create consistent guidance for common collection transformations while retaining native loops when they are clearer.

prompt_templates.title: Filter and Map a Slice
prompt_templates.prompt: Using samber/lo in Go 1.18, show how to filter even integers and map them to squares. Explain each return type.

prompt_templates.title: Find and Deduplicate Values
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor my slice logic with Find and Uniq. Preserve first-seen order and handle the case where no matching item exists.

prompt_templates.title: Group Records Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a samber/lo pipeline that groups users by age. Explain error handling and avoid Must outside application initialization.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Concurrent Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my collection pipeline for core, parallel, mutable, or iterator helpers. Discuss cancellation, shared state, allocations, readability, and native Go alternatives.

output_examples.input: Remove duplicate labels while preserving their original order.
output_examples.output: Use Uniq. It returns labels in first-seen order, such as alpha, beta, and gamma.

output_examples.input: Find the first invoice total above 100 and report whether it exists.
output_examples.output: Use Find. Return the matching value with a boolean so the caller handles the missing case.

output_examples.input: Parse a required startup timestamp and fail immediately on invalid input.
output_examples.output: Use Must around the parser only during initialization. Invalid input causes a panic, so avoid this pattern in request handling.

best_practices: Confirm examples against the samber/lo version recorded in go.mod.
Use Must only when failure should stop initialization.
Prefer clear native Go when a helper would hide control flow or allocation costs.
anti_patterns: Do not fetch and trust mutable remote documentation without reviewing its source and version.
Do not replace every loop with helpers when readability or performance becomes worse.
Do not use parallel helpers for shared mutable state without synchronization.

faq.question: Which Go version is required?
faq.answer: Go 1.18 or later is required because the library relies on generics.

faq.question: How do I add samber/lo?
faq.answer: Run the documented go get command, then verify and commit the resulting go.mod and go.sum changes.

faq.question: Should samber/lo replace every native loop?
faq.answer: No. Use helpers where they improve clarity, and retain loops when control flow or performance requirements are clearer.

faq.question: Does the remote function list match my installed release?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. The guide warns that it tracks the latest repository commit and may include unreleased changes.

faq.question: When should I use Must?
faq.answer: Must panics when an error or false condition occurs. Limit it to initialization paths where immediate failure is intentional.

faq.question: Does the guide fully explain parallel helpers?
faq.answer: No. It lists the parallel package but does not provide a complete synchronization or cancellation example.
